:::{#thm-poisson-rate-ratio}
#### Rate ratios in Poisson regression

In a Poisson regression model (@def-poisson-reg),
suppose covariate $x_j$ enters the linear predictor $\eta(\vx)$
only through the single term $\b_j x_j$
(no interactions or transformations involving $x_j$).
Let $\vx$ and $\vxs$ be two covariate patterns
that are identical except that $x_j = a$ and $x^*_j = b$.
Then

$$\rateratio(\vx : \vxs) = \expf{\b_j (a - b)}$$ {#eq-poisson-rate-ratio}

and for any common exposure magnitude $t > 0$,
the ratio of expected counts equals the same rate ratio:

$$\frac{\mu(\vx, t)}{\mu(\vxs, t)} = \rateratio(\vx : \vxs)$$

:::

::: proof
Because $\vx$ and $\vxs$ agree on every covariate except $x_j$,
every term of $\eta(\vx)$ except $\b_j x_j$ is shared with $\eta(\vxs)$:

$$
\ba
\eta(\vx) - \eta(\vxs)
&= \paren{\b_0 + \b_1 x_1 + \lds + \red{\b_j a} + \lds + \b_p x_p} \\
&\phantom{={}} - \paren{\b_0 + \b_1 x_1 + \lds + \red{\b_j b} + \lds + \b_p x_p}
&& \text{(substitute the linear predictor)} \\
&= \red{\b_j a} - \red{\b_j b}
&& \text{(cancel the shared terms)} \\
&= \red{\b_j (a - b)}
&& \text{(factor out } \b_j \text{)}
\ea
$$

Then the rate ratio is:

$$
\ba
\rateratio(\vx : \vxs)
&= \frac{\lambda(\vx)}{\lambda(\vxs)}
&& \text{(definition of rate ratio)} \\
&= \frac{\expf{\eta(\vx)}}{\expf{\eta(\vxs)}}
&& \text{(Poisson regression rate function)} \\
&= \expf{\eta(\vx) - \eta(\vxs)}
&& \text{(quotient rule for exponentials)} \\
&= \expf{\b_j (a - b)}
&& \text{(substitute the difference of linear predictors)}
\ea
$$

For the expected counts at a common exposure $t > 0$:

$$
\ba
\frac{\mu(\vx, t)}{\mu(\vxs, t)}
&= \frac{\lambda(\vx) \cdot t}{\lambda(\vxs) \cdot t}
&& \text{(Poisson regression mean function)} \\
&= \frac{\lambda(\vx)}{\lambda(\vxs)}
&& \text{(cancel } t > 0 \text{)} \\
&= \rateratio(\vx : \vxs)
&& \text{(definition of rate ratio)}
\ea
$$

:::
